You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

The patch fixes a memory leak in the `renesas_i3c_i3c_xfers()` function by using the `__free(kfree)` cleanup attribute to automatically free the allocated transfer structure when it goes out of scope. Two modifications are made in a single file:

1. **`drivers/i3c/master/renesas-i3c.c`** – An `#include <linux/cleanup.h>` is added to provide the cleanup attribute. The local variable `xfer` is declared using `__free(kfree)` so that `kfree(xfer)` is automatically called when the variable exits scope, eliminating the previous leak where the allocated `xfer` was never freed on success or error paths.

The relationship between the modifications: the header inclusion is required to enable the `__free(kfree)` attribute, which in turn ensures the memory allocated by `renesas_i3c_alloc_xfer()` is properly freed, fixing the memory leak. No other files are affected.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
xfer = renesas_i3c_alloc_xfer(i3c, 1);
</text>
<text>
return 0;
</text>
Reason:
The `renesas_i3c_alloc_xfer()` allocates memory for a new transfer structure. The function returns zero at the end without ever calling `kfree(xfer)` to release that memory. Since there is no deallocation on any exit path (including potential early returns if the allocation fails, which is already handled), every successful call to `renesas_i3c_i3c_xfers()` leaks the allocated structure.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
#include <linux/cleanup.h>
</text>
<text>
struct renesas_i3c_xfer *xfer __free(kfree) = renesas_i3c_alloc_xfer(i3c, 1);
</text>
Reason:
The `__free(kfree)` attribute, enabled by including `<linux/cleanup.h>`, automatically calls `kfree()` on `xfer` when the variable goes out of scope. This ensures the allocated memory is freed when the function returns (whether normally or via an error path), eliminating the memory leak. The declaration is now combined with the allocation, and the old separate `struct renesas_i3c_xfer *xfer;` line is removed.
